Incorporating the Beige Book strengthens the hawkish-but-gradual read of the March 2018 FOMC statement:

- Labor market: Beige Book reports widespread employment growth and very strong demand for qualified workers across districts, with employers raising wages. Wage growth has picked up and compensation was also influenced by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. These signals point to building wage/price pressures.
- Inflation outlook: The Beige Book’s wage acceleration aligns with the FOMC’s expectation that 12‑month inflation would move up toward 2%, reducing downside inflation risks.
- Credit conditions context (from SLOOS): Business credit remains easy (eased C&I standards and tighter spreads), suggesting additional gradual hikes are unlikely to choke off investment. Household credit shows some caution (tighter card standards, softer demand), and CRE tighter at the margin, which tempers—though does not overturn—the hawkish tilt.

Bottom line: Beige Book evidence of tight labor markets and rising wages nudges policy implications modestly more hawkish than the SLOOS-only read, while retaining a gradual path.
